item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong positive evidence across all six pillars, especially semiconductors, AI safety, drug-price negotiation, FAFSA modernization, and competition rules.\nThe clearest negative evidence was not neglect of infrastructure or education; it was trade protectionism and some short-term political framing around student debt relief.\nI did not find strong 2024 evidence that Biden broadly undermined infrastructure, health, or administrative capacity; the record is more “active state-building with some policy friction” than “capture or neglect.”","evidence":[{"title":"FACT SHEET: Biden-Harris Administration Announces Over $5 Billion from the CHIPS and Science Act for Research, Development, and Workforce","publisher":"U.S. Department of Commerce","date":"2024-02-09","url":"https://www.commerce.gov/news/fact-sheets/2024/02/fact-sheet-biden-harris-administration-announces-over-5-billion-chips-and?tblci=GiAfd5rVyHWWN0CUnTywsbUeEJ_gYStEgJOetn6Jbm_tayDJ91Uo6azzoJv09Ocp%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F","summary":"The administration said it would invest billions in semiconductor R&D, the National Semiconductor Technology Center, and workforce development to speed commercialization and strengthen domestic innovation capacity.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4","5B.3"]},{"title":"Biden-Harris Administration Announces Preliminary Terms with Micron to Onshore Leading-Edge Memory Chip Production in U.S. for First Time in Decades","publisher":"U.S. Department of Commerce","date":"2024-04-25","url":"https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/04/biden-harris-administration-announces-preliminary-terms-micron-onshore","summary":"Commerce framed CHIPS funding as unlocking large private capital, domestic fabs, supply-chain resilience, and tens of thousands of jobs. This is direct long-run investment and industrial-capacity building.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4","5B.3"]},{"title":"March 26, 2024 - Letter from Secretary Cardona regarding additional steps the Department has taken to support students, families, and institutions during the transition to the Better FAFSA","publisher":"U.S. Department of Education","date":"2024-03-26","url":"https://www.ed.gov/laws-and-policy/education-policy/key-policy-letters-signed-by-the-education-secretary-or-deputy-secretary/03262024-Better-FAFSA","summary":"The department said it updated FAFSA systems and procedures that had not been modernized in 40 years, expanding access to Pell grants and making the education-finance pipeline more functional.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.3"]},{"title":"Negotiating for Lower Drug Prices Works, Saves Billions","publisher":"CMS","date":"2024-08-15","url":"https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/press-releases/negotiating-lower-drug-prices-works-saves-billions","summary":"Medicare negotiated lower prices on 10 high-cost drugs, projecting large savings and lower out-of-pocket costs. That reduces a major health-cost drag on households and firms.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.3"]},{"title":"FTC Announces Rule Banning Noncompetes","publisher":"Federal Trade Commission","date":"2024-04-23","url":"https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2024/04/ftc-announces-rule-banning-noncompetes","summary":"The FTC said banning most noncompetes would raise worker mobility, make entry easier, and encourage new business formation.
